Pre-grade the 34 ungraded submissions of Assignment 4 using the rubric.

✅ Pre-grading complete — 34 submissions analysed.

**Summary**
- Mean score: **14.8/20** (class mean 15.2)
- Distribution: A: 6 · B+: 9 · B: 11 · C: 6 · D: 2
- **Plagiarism flags:** 3 submissions share >60% similarity (I’ve marked them for your review)
- **AI-suspicious:** 2 submissions show perfect structure with unusual time gaps

**Top insight:** Question 4 (Bellman-Ford application) explains most variance — 21 students lost ≥3 marks there. Consider a follow-up tutorial.

All 34 drafts are attached with per-criterion comments. Approve in bulk, or review individually — your call. I’ll apply your edits to the bank of grading decisions.
Build a 50-minute lesson plan on paging for Sec B (weaker batch).

Here’s a 50-minute plan calibrated to Sec B (avg internal 66):

**0–8 min — Hook:** “Why does your phone ‘run out of memory’ when you’re not using apps?” → introduce virtual memory with a live demo app.

**8–22 min — Core:** Page tables & address translation. Use the *book-index analogy* (page = chapter, offset = line). 3 worked examples on the board, class attempts the 4th.

**22–34 min — Hands-on:** Worksheet with 6 small translations; pair work. I can generate the worksheet — say the word.

**34–44 min — Common errors:** TLB misses, multi-level tables. Show 3 wrong answers from last year and crowdsource the fix.

**44–50 min — Exit ticket:** 2 MCQs (I’ll auto-generate and mark).

**Differentiation:** 4 extension questions for fast finishers; the worksheet has a scaffolded version.

savedLessonPlans.title: Network flows & max-flow/min-cut
objectives: State the max-flow min-cut theorem and its intuition
Compute augmenting paths using residual graphs
Relate flows to bipartite matching applications

sections.title: Introduction & hook
sections.content: Open with the "evacuation planning" problem: how much traffic can move through a road network in an hour? Elicit student guesses before revealing the abstraction.

sections.title: Core concept
sections.content: Define flow networks, capacity constraints, conservation. Walk through residual graphs and augmenting paths on a 5-vertex example (Ford–Fulkerson).

sections.title: Worked examples
sections.content: Example A: trace augmenting paths to max flow 14. Example B: find the min cut and verify max-flow = min-cut.

sections.title: Class discussion
sections.content: Why does greedy path choice fail? What happens with negative residual capacities? Discuss bipartite matching as a flow problem.

sections.title: Practice
sections.content: Pair work: solve the provided 6-vertex network sheet (2 problems). Peer check with the answer key.

savedLessonPlans.title: Deadlock detection & recovery
objectives: Identify the four necessary conditions for deadlock
Use the wait-for graph for detection

sections.title: Introduction & hook
sections.content: Show a real deadlock from a database log: two transactions holding each other's locks. What went wrong?

sections.title: Core concept
sections.content: The four conditions (mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait) with a running example.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Build a wait-for graph from a resource-allocation snapshot; detect the cycle; apply Banker's-algorithm-style checks.

sections.title: Case study
sections.content: Deadlock in a railway crossing / printer spooler scenario — groups propose detection + recovery plans.

sections.title: Practice & exit ticket
sections.content: 3 quick questions: classify each condition, find the cycle, choose recovery.
